# Props and the library

What a presentation sets down, and what a person keeps to use on any note: the library that keeps props and voices, the Dex that shows it, the Props card, the parts a scene gives any make to play, a prop refined into versions, and what every prop is made of. The plan and its status are [next/library.md](../next/library.md).

## The library

Library - what a person keeps to use on every note (next/library.md): one root, `user://library/`, a folder per shelf - `things/` (props, `ThingLibrary`) and `pictures/` (a prop's picture, named by the hash of what it is, `PropStudio`). `voices/`: voices kept for every note, each beside its sample (`VoiceLibrary`). Moved aside under test (`root`), so a gate never writes the author's library; what is removed goes to the system trash, as a note does (`trash`).

Source: [src/platform/library.gd](../src/platform/library.gd)

### Props kept

ThingLibrary - props kept to stand on any table (next/library.md): the library's `things` shelf (`Library`), one file per prop, `<slug>.json`: `{name, line, thing, materials, hash}`. A prop is kept by a person's choice, never automatically, and is the thing alone - its parts, its scale and the materials they use - never where it stood on the table it came from, its group or why it was there (`OWN`).

A prop refined is still one prop: its file keeps every version (`versions`, oldest first, `versions`) and which of them is used (`at`), and its own `thing`, `materials` and `hash` are that one's (`use_version`). A new version is added beside the rest and used only when a person says so (`add_version`); none is ever taken away. It is found as kept by the hash of any of its versions (`kept_as`, `hashes_of`), so the prop it was kept from is never kept again.

Put on a table (`put_on`) it is that thing again: named so no other thing there shares its name, each material it uses added under its own name, and renamed where the table has another of that name, so it looks the same on every table. A file from anywhere (one handed on, or edited by hand) comes in through `sanitized`, bounded as a made one is (`Props.sanitize`).

Source: [src/table/thing_library.gd](../src/table/thing_library.gd)

### Voices kept

VoiceLibrary - voices kept for every note (next/library.md): the library's `voices` shelf (`Library`), one file per voice, `<slug>.json`: `{name, line, hash, voice}`. A kept voice is who speaks and how (`OWN`): the model and its reader, a Kokoro blend or the formant voice, the tone, the pace, the pauses, the delivery dials, the ink, and how it sings (`SINGING`: what a composed Sound casting it reads). Where it is heard - the room (`ROOM`) - is never kept: it stays each note's, one narrator in a car and at a desk.

A note reads a kept voice by name (`kept:` on its row, `ReadingCast`) and carries a copy of what it last read. A voice renamed answers to its old names too (`was`), so the notes reading it follow it.

Its sample (`sample`): the opening of the Test passage said once in the voice, a WAV on the shelf named by what the voice sounds like (`sound_of`), so a rename keeps it and a change to the voice asks for another. The Voice card makes it (`maker`); `sampled` tidies the samples no voice names.

Every write refuses a session that may not write the library (`Library.writable`); `version` counts this process's writes, so whatever shows the shelf knows to look again. A file from anywhere comes in through `sanitized`, bounded: every number finite and in its dial's range, every text short, no path where a model is named.

Source: [src/voice/voice_library.gd](../src/voice/voice_library.gd)

## The Dex

DexWindow - the Dex: what the library keeps and what scenes build, a shelf at a time, a tile an entry. Its sections (`ShelfSection`) are props, voices, what can be round a scene and what scenes build when it is opened on its own (the bottom-right row's button), or the one section a card hands it ("+ Add a prop" on the Props card, a row's Choose…, "+ Add to the environment", whose section adds what is picked: Use). Its shelves are listed down its left side under the kind of thing each holds (Props, Voices, Environment: `ShelfSection.category`), each with how many it has. Each tile shows an entry's picture, its name (renamed in place where it can be), its line and its verbs - Use, Hear for a voice, Export… to hand it on in a file, and what its section offers besides; Import… takes such a file in. A filter by words narrows the shelf, opened with the words a section asks for (`ShelfSection.find`). Pictures are asked for in view and near it first (`ShelfSection.want_pictures`), every other on the shelf behind them (`ShelfSection.prepare_pictures`), and each is shown as it arrives; a click on a prop's opens it whole, in 3D (`PropViewer`). It opens centered in the room beside the side panel, never under it (`Shell.center_beside`). Escape or the window's close hides it.

Source: [src/ui/dex_window.gd](../src/ui/dex_window.gd)

ShelfSection - what one kind of thing the library keeps puts on the Dex's shelves (`DexWindow`): props, voices. The window draws, the section does; it names no component, and no component names the window. A presentation's Props card hands a `PropSection`, which is one of these with rows of its own.

An offer is one entry on a shelf: `{key, name, line, shelf, picture, sound, named, tip, verbs}` - `picture` an Image (null until it is taken), `sound` a playable file ("" for none), `named` whether its name can be changed in place (`rename`), `verbs` its buttons, each `{key, label, tip}` with `off` (grayed, `tip` saying why) where it applies, done by `act`. An offer that can be built whole is turned in 3D (`model_of`, `PropViewer`). These defaults offer nothing.

Source: [src/ui/shelf_section.gd](../src/ui/shelf_section.gd)

## The Props card

PropsCard - the panel's Props card: what the note's presentation sets down, one entry a prop (`EntryCard`) - its picture, its name and size, and a × that takes it off - under the groups its sections give (`PropSection`, handed by whatever shows props), and "+ Add a prop", which opens the Dex on the section's shelves (`DexWindow`). A click on an entry opens it: its Used tick, its verbs and its properties (`PropSection`'s `fields`, `SchemaForm`), each change handed to its section. A click on a picture opens the prop whole, in 3D, to be turned (`PropViewer`). Shown only while some section has a row or something to add. Looked at again every second (what a section has follows what is shown and made), and drawn again only when that changed. The Environment card's list is one of these.

Source: [src/ui/props_card.gd](../src/ui/props_card.gd)

### The 3D view

PropViewer - one prop whole, in 3D, in a window of its own: built as it stands (`PropSection.model_of`), lit as its picture is (`StudioLook`), and turned in the hand. A drag turns it about any axis (across the window about the upright, up and down about the level), a drag with Shift rolls it, the wheel brings it closer, a right or middle drag moves it, and a double click or "Set straight" puts it back as it opened. Opened by a click on a prop's picture on the Props card (`PropsCard`) or a shelf (`DexWindow`), centered beside the side panel (`Shell.center_beside`). Drawn only while it is shown; what it holds is let go when it closes. Escape or the window's close hides it.

A prop kept with versions (`PropVersions`) is stepped through here, ‹ and ›, and the one shown made the prop by Use this one; the section it was opened from follows (`PropSection.refined`). Refine… asks an agent to change the version shown as a person says (`PropRefine`): a prop not kept yet is kept first, and what the agent makes is shown as a new version, used only when chosen.

Source: [src/ui/prop_viewer.gd](../src/ui/prop_viewer.gd)

## Roles

PropMakes - the parts a scene gives a prop to play (a role: the desk's mug, its terminal, a phone), and the make chosen to play one, built (next/working_props.md). What a role does is the scene's - a mug is lifted to the mouth, a terminal shows its program on its screen - and any make of it is built in the role's frame so that holds: its foot on y = 0, centered, its front toward +z, its height within the role's (`made`). A scene works a make through its rig (`PropRig`: its faces, lights and named parts), never by its shapes.

A role's own make is a recipe drawn from the scene's number (`recipe`, `DeskLook.spec_of`) or a prop shipped with the app (`own`, a `.prop.json` as Export writes one). A choice is `{}` (the role's own), `{recipe, seed}` (its recipe drawn from another number), `{kept}` (a prop kept in the library by that name, `ThingLibrary`) or `{aside: true}` (taken off: a scene that lets the role go sets nothing out for it, and its picture is its own make's). A make missing a face the scene fills (`faces`) cannot play the role: the role's own plays it. The Dex offers makes (`MakeShelf`); the scene keeps the choice in its note.

Source: [src/desk/prop_makes.gd](../src/desk/prop_makes.gd)

## Refining a prop

LibraryVersions - the versions of the library's props, and refining one (`PropVersions`, `ThingLibrary`; next/library.md, "Refining a prop"). A prop is found kept by the hash of any of its versions, and one not kept yet is kept on its first refine. Refining hands the version shown to an agent - the writer a person picks (`AgentPick`) - with three pictures of it as built (`PropStudio.views`) and the author's direction, as rules/table/prop_refiner.yaml tells it; what it answers is added as a new version (`land`), never used until a person chooses it. One refining at a time; one given up adds nothing.

Source: [src/table_show/library_versions.gd](../src/table_show/library_versions.gd)

What the agent is told: [rules/table/prop_refiner.yaml](../rules/table/prop_refiner.yaml).

## What a prop is made of

Props: things built from a description. A thing is a few parts, each one shape with real sizes and one material whose surface is procedural (with an ornament worked into it if it has one), or a group of parts, placed and repeated as one (a candelabra's arm, cup and taper, copied round). An agent writes the description - centimeters, the thing's base on y = 0, its front toward +z - and `sanitize` makes whatever it wrote buildable; `build` makes the meshes, in meters.

Shapes, materials, plays and ornaments are registries, and their words are what an agent reads when it chooses (`describe`), so the prompt and the builder cannot disagree about what exists. Geometry is built here rather than from CSG nodes because a part's lobes, twist and wax drips displace it as it is built.

An agent draws its own curves - a lathe's profile, a tube's or a loft's path, an extrude's or a section's outline, any point of them rounded or kept crisp - and any part can be warped whole (bent, twisted, tapered, leaned, scaled, wobbled). It never writes vertices: typed by hand they come back inside out, holed and unshaded, and skip the foot and the heaps every built shape feeds. A smooth curve keeps a flat base and top flat (`_lathe`).

Source: [src/table/props.gd](../src/table/props.gd)

### Shapes (21)

A part is one of these (`Props.SHAPES`), as the set dresser reads them.

- **`lathe`** - a solid turned about the vertical axis, as on a lathe: vessels, candles, candlesticks, cups, bowls, bottles, vases, stems, bells, finials, coins. `profile`: [radius, height] points from the middle of the bottom outward and up the outside; a HOLLOW thing goes on over its rim and back down the inside to the middle of its inner floor - a bowl is [[0,0],[3,0],[6,4],[6.4,4.2],[5.8,4],[2.8,0.6],[0,0.6]]. Optional: `smooth` true curves through the points instead of joining them straight (a flat base and a flat top stay flat); a point written [radius, height, r] has its corner rounded r centimeters, and [radius, height, 0] keeps a crisp corner in a smooth profile - a foot, a rim, the edge where a lid sits; `sides` 3-12 cuts it flat-sided (6 is hexagonal); `lobes` bulges round it (a scalloped bowl, a melon, a fluted column) with `lobe_depth` 0.05-0.4; `twist` in degrees from bottom to top (a twisted taper). A candle's wax has `wick` true - its flame is lit at the middle of its top, which is melted into a shallow pool - or `wicks` 2-6, set round the top (three make a triangle), or `wicks` [[x, z], ...] placing each, centimeters from the middle; and `drips` 0-1.
- **`box`** - a block with rounded edges: books, boxes, tins, slabs, trays, a plinth. `size` [width, height, depth]; `round` the edges' radius; `taper` 0-0.9 narrows it toward the top.
- **`ball`** - a sphere, stretched to `size` [width, height, depth]: crystal balls, beads, fruit, eggs, orbs, pebbles, tumbled stones. `lumpy` 0-1 makes it irregular like a tumbled stone or a fruit; `facets` true cuts it into flat faces like a rough, raw stone.
- **`point`** - one crystal: a prism with a pointed end, standing up from its base - a tower, a single point. `radius`, `length` (the prism), `tip` (the point), `sides` (6 for quartz).
- **`cluster`** - a crystal cluster: points growing out of one rough rock. `count` 3-24, `radius` (the rock), `length` [shortest, longest], `spread` (degrees the outer points lean out), `thickness` (a point's width over its length, 0.1-0.3), `base` (the rock's material, if not the crystal's).
- **`geode`** - a geode broken open: a rough round rock, hollow, the hollow lined with crystal points growing in toward its middle. It lies open side up; `turn` [30, 0, 0] tips the opening toward the reader. `radius` (the rock's), `rind` (the thickness of its shell), `length` (the crystals'), `base` (the rock's material; plain gray rock if not given). The part's own material is the crystals'.
- **`ring`** - a ring lying flat round the vertical axis, resting on whatever is under it: rims, rings, bangles, a coiled rope. `radius` (to the middle of the band), `thickness` (the band's), `arc` (degrees, less than 360 for an open ring).
- **`tube`** - a round rod along a path: handles, stems, incense sticks, wands, branches, wire, a feather's quill, a pipe. `path` [[x,y,z], ...] in the thing's own space, `radius` (or `radii`, one per point, to taper or swell it). It curves through its points (`smooth` false: joined straight, every bend a crisp elbow, like a bent wire); a point written [x, y, z, r] bends round r centimeters there (a pipe's elbow), and [x, y, z, 0] is a crisp kink in a smooth path. `wall` (centimeters) makes it hollow and open at both ends: a pipe, a straw, a spout.
- **`loft`** - a form swept along a path through CROSS-SECTIONS that change as it goes - what a lathe, a tube or an extrude cannot make: a spout wide at the body and narrow at its lip, a blade of a snake plant or an aloe, a cactus pad, a horn, a spoon's handle, a shell's whorl, a curling leaf with real thickness. `path` [[x,y,z], ...] as a tube's (with its corners), or none: it rises straight up `height`. `sections` [{`at` 0-1 along the path, `outline` (as an extrude's, or `points` [[x, z], ...]), `size` [width, thickness] or one number, `sides`, `scale`, `turn` (degrees about the path), `shift` [x, z]}, ...]: the form blends smoothly from each section to the next (`smooth` false: straight); a section of `size` 0 closes to a point. Width runs across the path and thickness the other way - the thing's x and z while the path runs up. An outline, size or sides written on the part itself is every section's unless it says otherwise. `wall` makes it hollow and open at both ends.
- **`coil`** - a band wound round the vertical axis: an incense coil, a spring, a coiled cord, a curling tendril, a spiral of wire. `turns`, `radius` (where it starts) and `radius2` (where it ends: larger for a flat spiral), `height` (how far it climbs over all its turns; 0 lies flat), `thickness` (the band's, as a ring's).
- **`sheet`** - a thin flat piece lying on the cloth unless turned, placed by its middle: a leaf, a petal, a feather, a page, a scrap of cloth. `outline` (leaf, petal, feather, oval or rect - or `points` [[x,z], ...] for any outline), `size` [width, length] (its length runs front to back), `bend` -1..1 (the tip curls up), `fold` 0-1 (the sides lift).
- **`bloom`** - a flower head, petals in rings round a small middle: `petals`, `layers` 1-4, `radius`, `cup` 0 (open flat) to 1 (a closed bud), `width` (a petal's width over its length).
- **`strand`** - something long and limp laid down: a rope, a cord, a wire, a vine, a string of beads, a chain. `kind` (rope, cord, wire, vine, beads or chain), `length` (centimeters along it), `thickness` (how wide it is), and how it lies, `lay`: "coil" (coiled down, loop piled on loop, as a rope is - `radius` the loops'), "flemish" (wound flat in a spiral from the middle out), "heap" (dropped in a loose tangle, crossing over itself - within `radius`), "path" (laid along `path` [[x, z], ...], centimeters from the thing's middle, its length the path's) or "drape" (laid across the table itself and over its edge - DRAPED, below). `loose` 0-1: how unkempt it lies, 0 laid neatly, 1 thrown down. A vine carries leaves - `leaf` their length (centimeters) and `leaves` their material, if not the stem's. It rests on the cloth, and on itself wherever it crosses itself.
- **`bone`** - a bone, lying on its side along x: `kind` "femur" (a thigh bone: a ball on a neck at one end, two knuckles at the other), "long" (an arm or leg bone, knobbed at both ends), "rib" (a curved, flattened bar), "small" (a chicken's or a small animal's - thin, knobbed, a little bent: copy it in a `heap` for a pile of them) or "wishbone"; `length` and `thickness` (the shaft's, centimeters). Its material is most often `bone`.
- **`skull`** - a skull, resting on its jaw and facing the thing's front: `kind` "human", "horned" (a cow's, a goat's or a ram's, long-snouted, with `horns` "straight", "curved" or "curled", or "none") or "bird" (a long beak); `length` (centimeters, front to back - a person's is about 19). Its sockets are deep and its openings go through. It is bone, not a head: no eyes, no skin, nothing living.
- **`sculpt`** - a form modeled freely, as clay is, from STROKES - for what no other shape makes: the skull or the jaw of a creature not listed, a shell, an antler, a gnarled root, a seed pod, a mushroom, a stone worn into a shape, a carved charm. `strokes` [{`points` [[x, y, z, r], ...]}, ...] in order: each stroke a rod through its points (curving through them; `smooth` false joins them straight), r its thickness there (a radius, centimeters), so it swells and narrows as it goes; one point is a ball, stretched to `size` [width, height, depth] if given. Each stroke melts into what came before it, `blend` centimeters soft (0 a crisp seam); `carve` true cuts it out of what came before instead - a socket, a groove, a hollow, a hole right through, the gap under an arch. `mirror` true makes it the same on both sides of x = 0: draw only its middle and its right side. It is one surface, its hollows shut in from the light; a rod much thinner than a hundredth of the whole comes out broken. Draw it blind and you will not get it right first: look at it from every side, and put it again.
- **`mask`** - A FACE WITH NO ONE IN IT, life size or any size: a mask form, a makeup artist's practice face, a mannequin's face, a milliner's block - its eyes closed, its lips closed, no hair and no ears, smooth all over, standing on its chin and facing the thing's front (+z). `size` [width, height, depth] (a person's: [15, 21, 8] - depth from its rim to the tip of its nose), `relief` 0.3-1.5 (how strongly its features stand out: 1 a person's), `thick` (its flat back's depth behind its rim, centimeters). Stand it on a stand or prop it against something: it has no foot of its own. Give it `skin` true to paint its face.
- **`tuft`** - A BRUSH'S HAIRS: a bundle of fine hairs rising from y = 0 (where they leave the ferrule) to their tips, which bend as the brush is pulled and pressed and spring back as it lifts. `kind` round (a soft point), liner (long and fine), flat (a chisel edge, wide across x), fan (spread wide), dome (full and rounded - a blending or powder brush) or bud (a cotton swab's tip: short, dense and rounded, barely bending - it lays no paint, it lifts a small or faint spill of fresh paint); `length` (centimeters out of the ferrule), `width` (across, at the ferrule), `thick` (a flat or fan's thinness), `hairs` (6-140). Build a brush as a group: a `tube` handle, a short `lathe` or `loft` ferrule, and the tuft standing out of it - give the group a free `joint` and `points` {"tip": the tuft's end, "grip": the handle's} so it can be picked up and painted with. A cotton swab is a thin `tube` stick with a bud tuft at its end, built the same way.
- **`grains`** - LOOSE STUFF, poured and never one piece: sand, salt, sugar, snow, ash, flour, seeds, peppercorns, ground herbs, tea, powder, gravel, beads. Drawn where it lies, `at` inside the vessel that holds it - it fills that vessel's inside from the bottom up to `fill` (0-1 of the way to its rim), capped at 240 grains without enlarging them - or on the cloth or a dish, where it lies in a little heap of `amount` grains (up to 240). `grain`: one grain's size in centimeters (0.1 sugar or flour, drawn as small clumps, to 1 a pea or a bead); its material is its look, and how it behaves - heavy or light, whether it dissolves. An empty receiving vessel needs no grains part: what is poured into it arrives from the source. It is REAL: tipped, its vessel spills it from the mouth and it falls, runs and heaps where it lands, and in a liquid it sinks, floats or dissolves.
- **`extrude`** - an outline raised straight up: trays, tiles, plaques, tablets, boxes, dishes and candles of any plan - a star, a hexagon, a heart. `outline` (polygon with `sides` 3-12, star with `sides` points, circle, rect, heart, lens (pointed at both ends, as a leaf or an eye is) or drop (round behind, pointed in front) - or `points` [[x, z], ...] for any outline, which may go in and out), `size` [width, depth], `height`; optional `taper` 0-0.9 (narrower at the top), `bevel` (centimeters cut off the top edge), `wall` (centimeters: hollow, as a tray or a dish is, its floor as thick as its wall). A wax extrude takes `wick` or `wicks` as a turned candle does.
- **`face`** - A FACE THAT SHOWS SOMETHING: a flat panel, upright, facing the thing's front (+z), placed by its middle - the glass of a screen, a dial's card, a meter's scale, a label, a sticker. `size` [width, height]; `outline` rect, round (a disc or an ellipse - a round scope) or rounded (`round` its corners' radius); `turn` [-90, 0, 0] lays it face up. What it shows is the scene's, handed by the part's `name` (a terminal's `screen`, a radar's `scope`); with nothing handed it is its material - a dark glass, a white card. `lit` 0-1: how much it shines by itself (a screen, a lit dial) rather than by the room's light. `glass`, how a screen shows its picture: `curve` 0-0.3 (a tube's bulge), `lines` 0-1 (scanlines) and `line_count`, `bloom` 0-2 (a phosphor's glow round what is lit), `mono` 0-1 (black and white), `snow` 0-1, `brightness`. `text`: words printed or written on it, as large as fit (`hand` print, marker or type; `ink` their color) - a scene may hand it other words by its name.

### Materials (18)

Each part's surface is one material (`Props.MATERIALS`), procedural.

| Material | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `metal` | brass, copper, bronze, silver, iron, pewter, gold; `wear` is tarnish or patina in `color2`, `pattern` a hammered surface |
| `wax` | candle wax - beeswax, paraffin, tallow; `clarity` how much the light glows through it |
| `glass` | see-through; `color` tints it, a low `clarity` frosts it, an ornament on glass is etched |
| `crystal` | quartz, amethyst, citrine, obsidian, selenite, any mineral; `clarity` from milky 0 to water-clear 1, `pattern` banding in `color2` - curving round in rings with `rings` true (agate, malachite, onyx) |
| `ceramic` | glazed or bare clay - porcelain, stoneware, terracotta, faience; `polish` is the glaze, `pattern` speckle, `wear` crazing, `color2` where the glaze pools |
| `stone` | marble, slate, granite, soapstone, alabaster, jasper; `pattern` veins in `color2` - curving round in rings with `rings` true (banded jasper) - and `wear` flecks |
| `wood` | any timber, carved or turned; `pattern` its grain in `color2`, `polish` oil or varnish |
| `paper` | paper, card, parchment; `wear` stains in `color2` |
| `leather` | hide and leather bindings; `wear` scuffs in `color2` |
| `fabric` | cloth, velvet, silk, cord; `polish` is a velvet's sheen |
| `bone` | bone, ivory, horn, shell; `wear` yellows it toward `color2` |
| `plant` | leaves, petals, stems, herbs; `wear` dries them toward `color2` |
| `liquid` | what is IN a vessel - a brew, ink, oil, wine, water, honey - wet and never quite still, `pattern` its foam in `color2`, `clarity` the light in its depth; a part of its own filling the vessel to its surface (see WORKING PARTS: it boils, fills, empties, changes color and glows) |
| `powder` | loose fine stuff, and what is ground: snow, flour, ash, chalk, salt, sugar, pollen, ground spice, dust - matte and soft, `pattern` the sparkle of the grains that catch the light (snow, salt, sugar) in `color2`; its grains dissolve in a liquid in `dissolves` seconds (snow melts in 2, sugar in 6, salt in 10; 0 never - ash, sand) |
| `cream` | a soft paste in a pot or a stick - greasepaint, cream makeup, a lipstick, a balm, frosting, butter, wax polish: smooth and a little waxy, `polish` its sheen, `pattern` the swirls a finger or a brush has left in its top; what a tool is loaded with paint from |
| `sponge` | soft foam full of fine holes - a makeup sponge, a sea sponge, a foam wedge, a powder puff's face: matte, `pattern` how open its pores are, `wear` the paint soaked into it in `color2`; it gives where it is pressed |
| `plastic` | molded plastic, its color all through - a computer's case, a phone, a keyboard's keys, a knob, a toy; `polish` its sheen (satin low, glossy high), `wear` scuffs and the yellowing of age toward `color2` |
| `painted` | lacquer, enamel or paint over anything |

### Ornaments (10)

Worked into a part's surface (`Props.ORNAMENTS`).

| Ornament | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `bands` | raised rings round it, `count` of them |
| `flutes` | grooves running up it, `count` round |
| `dots` | a field of dots, `count` round |
| `stars` | five-pointed stars, `count` round |
| `moons` | crescent moons, `count` round |
| `zigzag` | one zigzag band, `count` peaks round |
| `scales` | overlapping scales, `count` round |
| `spiral` | lines winding up it, `count` of them |
| `lattice` | a diamond lattice, `count` diamonds round |
| `hammered` | the dimpled face of hand-hammered metal, all over |

### Plays of light (6)

What moves in a material as it turns (`Props.PLAYS`).

| Play | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `silk` | a silky band of light lying across its fibers, sliding over it as it turns; `pattern` stripes it in `color2` - tiger's eye, hawk's eye, satin spar selenite |
| `flash` | broad patches that flash `color2` and the colors beside it where they catch the light, dark elsewhere - labradorite, spectrolite |
| `fire` | small patches of every color, changing as it turns - opal |
| `glitter` | tiny flakes of `color2` that sparkle in the flames - goldstone, sunstone, aventurine, the pyrite in lapis |
| `rainbow` | an oily rainbow film over the surface - aura quartz, rainbow obsidian, bismuth, paua, abalone, mother of pearl |
| `glow` | a soft light of `color2` floating under the surface - moonstone |
